findings.message: This is a class fix for the round-2 B3 finding. A malformed AMAX_BASE_URL (or any invalid env) now throws from loadEnv(). An unset AMAX_BASE_URL in production warns once. All three callers (welcome page, robots.ts, sitemap.ts) share the path, and tests cover unset, set, malformed and foreign-host cases. The remaining issue is how it was fixed: knownOrigin() repeats baseUrl()'s rules (`env.AMAX_BASE_URL`, `NODE_ENV !== "production"`, the LOOPBACK test) so it can predict when baseUrl() will throw. The two copies agree today. If baseUrl() later accepts another host or environment and knownOrigin()'s condition isn't updated, the page silently drops its canonical URL while OAuth works. Fix: have baseUrl() return or throw a typed "unset" result (or export a single `resolveOrigin()` that returns `{origin} | {unset}`), and keep only the warn-once in knownOrigin().
findings.scenario: Someone changes baseUrl() to accept a staging host without AMAX_BASE_URL → OAuth metadata uses it, but knownOrigin() still returns null, so /welcome has no canonical URL and sitemap.xml is empty.

findings.message: This is a class fix for the round-2 AC-3 finding. Planned work is now data (`coming: Planned[]` with a module id), every Coming item is checked as not installed, and the hero and description copy moved into copy.ts. Today's copy shows no current violation. The prose guard, though, only scans HERO_LEDE, DESCRIPTION and the live claims. The rest of the page's copy is unchecked: Problem, HowItWorks step bodies, Trust, ChatPreview, Closing, the ProductVideo figcaption and captions file, the page TITLE and OG image alt, and the Features heading ("One system for delivery, people and money"). The word list also misses obvious variants such as "pay run", "finance" and "invoice list". Fix: move all marketing prose into copy.ts (or scan the rendered page in marketing.spec.ts), and run the same Coming-words check over all of it.
findings.scenario: An edit to HowItWorks adds "payroll runs itself" → marketing-areas.test.ts stays green, and the page claims an unshipped module (the AC-3 defect again).

findings.message: The 062 mock section (copied from .specclaw/mock/index.html) still has the copy this round removed from the code. The hero says "Payroll, leave and billing stay up to date through chat". The "People and payroll" tile is marked Coming, while "Finance and sales" and "Operations" are shown as live. Code and mock now disagree on AC-3. Separately, the nav and CTA links use `onclick="document.getElementById(\'mk-features\')…"`: inside an HTML attribute the backslashes are literal, so the handler is a JS syntax error and the links do nothing. Fix: bring the mock section in line with HERO_LEDE and AREAS, and use plain `href="#mk-features"` anchors.
findings.scenario: A reviewer compares the mock with /welcome: the mock offers payroll and billing as live and its Features link does nothing; the shipped page marks both Coming.

findings.message: The 062 mock section, which is the design doc for this page, still has the copy this round removed from the shipped page. The hero still says 'Payroll, leave and billing stay up to date through chat'. The 'Finance and sales', 'Operations' and 'Platform' tiles list contracts, billing, expenses, Xero/QuickBooks, IT assets and access with no 'Coming' mark, and 'People and payroll' is shown as wholly Coming. So the mock and apps/web/components/marketing now disagree. The mock is read-only during a build, so update .specclaw/mock in its own small change to match copy.ts and areas.ts.
findings.scenario: A reviewer compares the page against the mock and sees payroll and billing as live in the mock but Coming on the page.
